answer: Sequential work logging: each identity must complete a chain of timed micro-tasks, each signed with a hardware beacon that proves continuous participation. Reputation accrues only along verified chains, so cloned identities start from zero every time. An attacker cloning N agents must fund N parallel hardware chains plus idle-time costs before any agent gains trust — roughly linear cost per clone, no shortcut. Like timber grain, history can't be faked cheaply. The fable here is simple: fresh clones stay economically invisible until they've paid full participation price.
